# Attribution and provenance

This directory holds the complete three-term proof that passed on AutoLab (private hill
`koerbser/erdos-3-three-term`, experiment 751f08e4: only the standard axioms). The 44
plby/lean-proofs files are **not included**, because that repository has no license: run
`python fetch_plby.py` to download them at the pinned commit and apply the one documented
change. APAP and AddCombi (Apache-2.0) are included with their licenses and the modification
notices below.

`Solution.lean` proves `Erdos3ThreeTerm.Statement`, the three-term case of Erdős Problem 3
(formal-conjectures' `Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.three`). The mathematical input is the Kelley–Meka
bound on three-term-progression-free sets. It enters through the theorem `Erdos140.erdos_140` of
Boris Alexeev's formalization, which is vendored here together with the parts of APAP and
AddCombi that it imports.

These 78 files are the complete import closure of `ErdosProblems.Erdos140` with two exceptions:
Mathlib, which the hill image provides, and `APAP.Prereqs.DummyPositivity`, which is not vendored
(see below). Each file keeps its upstream module path, and the first two lines of each file name
its source and commit.

* **plby/lean-proofs.** GitHub reports no license for this repository, and none is granted for
  its own files. Its `src/latest/LICENSE` says only that "some files in this repository are from
  external sources and are licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0". None of the 44
  vendored files has such a header. They are included solely so that this private verification
  can run. All credit belongs to Boris Alexeev and to the authors named in the file headers:
  informal proof by Zachary Kelley and Raghu Meka; formal authors listed as Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol.
  Do not redistribute these files without the author's permission.
* **APAP** (Arithmetic Progressions, Almost Periodicity) formalizes the Bloom–Sisask exposition of
  the Kelley–Meka bound. It is licensed under Apache-2.0; the upstream `LICENSE` is copied
  unchanged to `APAP/LICENSE`. There is no upstream NOTICE file.
* **AddCombi** is licensed under Apache-2.0; the upstream `LICENSE` is copied unchanged to
  `AddCombi/LICENSE`. There is no upstream NOTICE file.
* **Mathlib** and **formal-conjectures** (both Apache-2.0) are not vendored; they come from the
  hill image. `Erdos3ThreeTerm.Statement` is supplied by the hill.

## Modifications (Apache-2.0 §4(b) notice)

Every vendored file begins with a two-line comment giving its source path and commit. That comment
also says whether the file was modified. Apart from that comment, the changes below are the only
ones. No declaration was renamed, restated or reproved.

1. **Lakefile options.** Plain `lean -o` does not read a lakefile, so the Lean options that each
   upstream lakefile sets for its own modules are repeated after the imports, with a one-line
   comment:
   * all 44 plby files get `set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false` and
     `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3`;
   * all 34 APAP and AddCombi files get `set_option autoImplicit false` and
     `set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false`.

   Options that only affect linting or pretty-printing are not repeated.
2. **All 34 APAP/AddCombi files: conversion from the module system to old-style files.**
   * The `module` line is deleted.
   * `public import X` becomes `import X`.
   * `public section` and `@[expose] public section` become `section`.
   * The `public` modifier is dropped from 7 declarations in `APAP/Physics/AlmostPeriodicity.lean`.
   * The `@[expose]` attribute is dropped: 1 standalone line in
     `APAP/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finrank.lean`; `@[expose] noncomputable def mu` in
     `APAP/Prereqs/Mu.lean`; `@[expose, simps]` becomes `@[simps]` in
     `APAP/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/AddChar.lean`; `@[expose, simps! -isSimp]` becomes
     `@[simps! -isSimp]` in `APAP/Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/FiniteAbelian/PontryaginDuality.lean`.
   * `meta def` becomes `def` for the three sound Lp-norm positivity extensions `evalDLpNorm`,
     `evalCLpNorm` and `evalWLpNorm` (in `APAP/Prereqs/LpNorm/{Discrete/Defs,Compact,Weighted}.lean`).
3. **`APAP/Physics/DRC.lean` and `APAP/Physics/Unbalancing.lean`.** The bare identifier `sqrt`
   becomes `Real.sqrt`: 11 occurrences on original lines 111, 179, 181, 183, 184, 186 and 192 of
   DRC, and 8 on original lines 144, 151, 152, 154 and 156 of Unbalancing. Under `open Real` these
   already meant `Real.sqrt`, so the elaborated terms do not change. The edit only prevents
   ambiguity with Mathlib's `RCLike.sqrt` when `Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Sqrt` is in scope.
   Without it, a check against the full Mathlib reported "Ambiguous term sqrt" on DRC lines 179,
   181, 183 and 192 and on Unbalancing lines 151, 152 and 154.
4. **`APAP/Prereqs/Convolution/Order.lean`.** Removed are the `import APAP.Prereqs.DummyPositivity`
   line (original line 5) and original lines 107–180. Those lines hold the three positivity
   extensions `evalConv`, `evalDConv` and `evalIterConv` (for `f ∗ᵈ g`, `f ○ᵈ g` and `f ∗ᵈ^ n`),
   plus the 10 `example`s that only test them. Upstream marks the extensions "TODO: Make it sound
   again"; they build their proofs from the 14 `sorry` lemmas of `APAP.Prereqs.DummyPositivity`.
   Every lemma in the file is kept. `APAP/Prereqs/DummyPositivity.lean` is therefore not vendored,
   and the submission contains no `sorry`.
5. **`APAP/Prereqs/Mu.lean`, comment only.** On original line 219, inside a commented-out Lean 3
   block, one Lean 3 keyword that the hill's token filter rejects was removed.

## Why removing the dummy positivity extensions is safe

Before the edit, the unsound extensions were active in 13 modules:
`APAP.Prereqs.Convolution.Order`, `APAP.Physics.DRC` and the plby modules `Sifting`,
`DensityStep`, `ConcreteSupply`, `FinalAssembly`, `BalancedRestrictionAssembly`, `GroupCount`,
`HolderApproximation`, `KelleyMekaCount`, `RawSupplyNumerics`, `TwoBohrBalanced` and
`ErdosProblems.Erdos140`.

An extension fires only when `positivity` meets a function-level convolution: as the goal, as a
factor, or inside an unweighted norm `‖f‖_[p]` or `‖f‖ₙ_[p]`, whose extensions recurse into `f`.
`positivity` is also the side-goal discharger of `gcongr`, `bound` and `field_simp`.

* No declaration outside `DummyPositivity.lean` and the extensions mentions a `dummy_*` lemma.
* In those 13 modules, I read every `positivity`, `gcongr`, `bound` and `field_simp` call inside a
  declaration that mentions a convolution (62 calls). Each goal is a scalar, a pointwise value
  `(f ○ᵈ g) x`, or a weighted norm `‖f‖_[p, w]`. None of these reaches the extensions: pointwise
  values don't match the extension keys, and the weighted-norm extension does not recurse.
* Wherever upstream needed nonnegativity of a convolution, it proves it explicitly (for example
  with `dddconv_nonneg mu_nonneg mu_nonneg`) and leaves `-- positivity` in a comment.

If I missed a case, the build now fails at that `positivity` call instead of silently depending on
`sorryAx`. The honest fix would then be the sound lemmas of the same file: `ddconv_nonneg`,
`dddconv_nonneg`, `ddconv_pos`, `iterConv_nonneg` and so on.

## `Solution.lean`

`Solution.lean` was written for this submission. It contains the dyadic reduction from AutoLab
experiment `6a9181bf` of `koerbser/erdos-3-attempt-3` (used here for `k = 3`), and Track B's bridge
`maxCard 3 N ≤ addRothNumber (Finset.Icc 1 N)` with its summation. Both were first checked as
`have`s inside one proof of the hill `erdos-3`. Here they are top-level lemmas with the same
statements and proofs, in namespace `Erdos3ThreeTermProof`, and they use `Erdos140.erdos_140`
directly.

"""Fetch the 44 plby/lean-proofs files that the three-term proof imports.

Boris Alexeev's repository (https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs) has no license,
so its files are not included here. This script downloads them at the commit the
verification used and applies the only change made to them: after the imports,
it repeats the two Lean options that plby's lakefile sets for its modules, since
compiling with plain `lean -o` reads no lakefile.

Usage: python fetch_plby.py [output_dir]   (default: this directory)
"""

import pathlib
import sys
import urllib.request

COMMIT = "8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e"
BASE = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/{COMMIT}/src/latest/"
BLOCK = [
    "-- plby's lakefile sets these leanOptions for all its modules; plain `lean -o` has no lakefile.",
    "set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false",
    "set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3",
    "",
]

here = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
out_dir = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else here

for rel in (here / "plby_files.txt").read_text().split():
    text = urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + rel).read().decode("utf-8")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    last_import = max((i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith("import ")), default=-1)
    header = [
        f"-- Fetched from https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs at commit {COMMIT}, file `src/latest/{rel}`.",
        "-- MODIFIED: the Lean options of plby's lakefile are repeated after the imports (see ATTRIBUTION.md).",
    ]
    result = header + lines[: last_import + 1] + BLOCK + lines[last_import + 1 :]
    target = out_dir / rel
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_text("\n".join(result) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("fetched", rel)
